spots.n: Skana The Spa at Turning Stone
spots.s: The resort's serious spa, with Oneida-inspired treatments and a quiet pool lounge; book a couples' massage and make a whole afternoon of it.
Three championship courses on resort grounds, PGA Tour pedigree included; Shenendoah is the easiest to get a tee time on and still a real test.
A 5,000-seat arena that books touring headliners, comedy and boxing; dinner downstairs, show upstairs, no driving in between.
An old-school lakeside midway with the Laffland dark ride and a Ferris wheel over Oneida Lake; ride at sunset, then walk the beach.
A long sand beach on Oneida Lake's east end with woodland trails behind it, the closest real beach day to Turning Stone.
Two glacial lakes so turquoise they look filtered; the 3-mile loop around Green Lake is CNY's classic walk-and-talk date.
A 167-foot cascade over Onondaga limestone with a short gorge trail and footbridge; at its best after rain or in October color.

spots.n: Old Erie Canal State Historic Park
spots.s: Thirty-six flat miles of towpath from DeWitt to Rome along the original 1825 canal; rent bikes or just walk the Chittenango Landing stretch.
A full-scale rebuilt Revolutionary War fort in downtown Rome, free to enter, with rangers in period dress and a good museum below.
Utica's Philip Johnson-designed art museum, with Pollock, Picasso and Cole in the galleries and the Fountain Elms mansion next door.
A small, walkable hillside zoo in Roscoe Conkling Park, red pandas and all; an easy, low-pressure daytime date.
America's second-oldest family brewery; the tour ends with tastings, and the 1888 Biergarten next door handles round two.
The 93-room home of a 19th-century utopian commune that famously went on to make silverware; the guided tours are full of odd stories.
The Oneida Indian Nation's hand-hewn white pine cultural center, with free exhibits on Oneida history and work by Haudenosaunee artisans.
One of the country's biggest malls, with go-karts, ropes courses, an IMAX and late-night restaurants for the rainy-day plan.
Syracuse's brick-warehouse district of restaurants, cocktail bars and boutiques; dinner, a speakeasy and a stroll, all on a few blocks.
A plunge-basin meromictic lake ringed by limestone cliffs, with short, dramatic trails just south of Syracuse.
One of the state's largest trout hatcheries, free to tour; see the raceways, feed the brookies, then fish the stocked water nearby.
A peninsula park on a quiet reservoir north of Rome with a beach, lakeside campsites and good shore fishing for bass and walleye.
U-pick apples in season and the 1911 cider and spirits tasting room up the hill; fall's most reliable afternoon date in CNY.
Utica's restored 1928 Mexican Baroque movie palace, now hosting Broadway tours, concerts and comedy; the lobby alone is worth dressing up for.
An 1807 Federal-style mansion and gardens on Cazenovia Lake, steps from a postcard village of cafes and shops made for an unhurried afternoon.
L. Frank Baum's birthplace pays tribute with a gloriously nerdy Oz collection; follow the actual yellow-brick sidewalk to get there.
At the far edge of the map but worth the drive; pair it with Cooperstown's Main Street and a lakeside dinner on Otsego Lake.

events.s: Alicia Keys' Broadway musical about coming of age in 1990s Manhattan, on tour at the Landmark Theatre.
Blues-rock guitar slinger Samantha Fish brings her Paper Doll tour, with Sgt. Splendor, to the Showroom.
Round two of the I-90 rivalry eight days later, back at the Adirondack Bank Center.
An in-state nonconference matchup as the Orange host Cornell at the JMA Wireless Dome.
The ventriloquist and his cast of puppets play Utica's Stanley Theatre.

events.n: New York State Craft Brewers Festival
events.s: A tasting session pouring beers from craft breweries around the state, inside the Landmark Theatre.
Central New York's two-mile drive-through holiday light show along Onondaga Lake, nightly 5–10p; buy tickets online ahead.
Syracuse Stage's holiday-season production of the epic musical, directed by Robert Hupp.
Thanksgiving-weekend season finale as the Orange host Notre Dame at the JMA Wireless Dome; kickoff time set 12 days out.

events.n: Lindsey Stirling: The Snow Waltz Tour
events.s: The dancing violinist's holiday show of electronic-meets-classical arrangements at the Landmark Theatre.

events.n: Straight No Chaser: Making Spirits Bright
events.s: The a cappella group's holiday tour stops at the Landmark Theatre.
Three performances of the holiday ballet at the Stanley Theatre (7p Fri–Sat, 2p Sun).

events.n: Derek Hough: Dance for the Holidays
events.s: The Dancing with the Stars pro's holiday dance spectacular in Turning Stone's Event Center.
A Central New York neighbor comes to the JMA Wireless Dome for nonconference basketball.
A holiday rock-opera show in the Trans-Siberian Orchestra vein, in the Showroom.
The Rodgers & Hammerstein classic on tour for a week of holiday-season shows at the Landmark Theatre.
New York club comic Mark Normand headlines the Event Center.
The former Staind frontman's country project closes out the year at the Event Center.
Multi-platinum Texas country-rock in the Showroom — 'Crazy Girl' and 'Drunk Last Night' sung back at full volume by a casino-weekend crowd.
Johnny Cash & June Carter tribute in the Turning Stone Showroom — Eric Hofmanis and Megan Houde run through 50 years of the duets and the Folsom-era hits.
Fab Four tribute night at the Stanley with the holiday songbook folded in — an easy Utica weeknight before the dance floors open.
A costumed orchestra plays Metallica, Queen and Zeppelin by the glow of hundreds of candles on the Stanley's stage — a surprisingly good date night.
The AGT crooner from Long Island brings his big-band swing and Sinatra standards to the Stanley for a Sunday matinee — Utica's Italian crowd turns out.
The Broadway Utica touring season brings the circus-set musical to the Stanley for two nights — acrobats, puppetry and a live Depression-era big top.
The touring Nutcracker with its international cast, 10-foot puppets and acrobats lands at the Landmark for one Saturday matinee.
Baz Luhrmann's 1996 film screened at the Landmark with the score played live by a full orchestra — Radiohead and Garbage cues included.
Join us for a happy hour in Utica! Friday from 6p with Mohawk Valley Outdoors at Nail Creek Pub, Utica · no Meetup fee.
A full-band Bee Gees tribute brings the disco-era catalog and the early ballads to the Stanley Theatre's 1928 movie-palace stage in downtown Utica.

The lakeside village turns Victorian for its 33rd season: an opening-day parade at noon on 11/27, then costumed Dickens characters, sing-alongs and roasted chestnuts downtown every Sat and Sun, noon–4p. Free.
A string ensemble plays 90s hip-hop staples by candlelight in Palladian Hall at the Treasury, a former bank hall on South Salina St in downtown Syracuse. A 60-minute set; doors open 45 minutes ahead.
The Thruway rivalry moves west: the Crunch host the Comets in AHL play at Upstate Medical University Arena, the War Memorial in downtown Syracuse.
Turning Stone's nightlife complex in Verona runs one countdown across its rooms: live bands at Turquoise Tiger and Tin Rooster, DJs at The Gig and NY Rec & Social Club. Ticketed, with VIP tables.
The marquee ACC home date of the winter: the Orange host Duke at the JMA Wireless Dome on the Syracuse University hill, the kind of night that fills the building.

nightlife.s: The region's big night out: table games, poker room and slots under one roof, with the Exit 33 bars a short walk away.
Turning Stone's main nightlife room for cover bands and touring DJs, with the biggest dance floor in the building on weekends.
A film-noir lounge at Exit 33 with handcrafted cocktails and live sets; the move for a dressed-up drink before the tables.
Nashville-style honky tonk with live country, line dancing and pit-fired BBQ; even skeptics end up on the floor.
Lava's old space reborn as a sportsbook lounge with a wall of LED screens, pool and darts, and resident DJs on weekends.
The Oneida Nation's Oz-themed casino in Chittenango, with the Winged Monkey bar open till 2 on weekends and a big sportsbook lounge.
Oneida Lake's casino, freshly doubled in size with a new hotel and The Lounge with Caesars Sports; a low-key pairing with a Sylvan Beach day.
Harness racing out back and slots inside; summer race nights with a drink trackside are a fun, unpretentious date.
A Hanover Square lounge with DJs Thursday through Saturday, cocktails and tacos, and a dance floor that fills after 11.
Armory Square's dance club in the neighborhood's original nightclub building, with weekend DJs, bottle service and a dress code to match.
Industrial-chic raw bar and steakhouse that dims the lights and brings in DJs as the night goes on; dinner and drinks without moving.
Through a back corridor off The Hops Spot: fish-scale tile bar, tufted booths, fresh-juice cocktails and live music on weekends.
An Art Deco basement bar beneath Oh My Darling, across from the Landmark Theatre, with live jazz and soul on Friday and Saturday nights.
Downtown's newer club and concert room, mixing touring acts with themed dance nights and raves; check the calendar and go.
A converted 1919 movie house that books hip-hop, R&B and dancehall acts alongside jam bands; general admission, so get close.
Armory Square's funk, soul and indie room, with chicken and waffles served until the band starts.
Utica's original craft beer pub, anchoring the Varick Street bar crawl; busiest around 10 on a Saturday.

eats.s: Turning Stone's only full-time sushi bar: nigiri, maki and sushi stacks, plus shoyu ramen and pho. Dinner only, Thu–Sun.
Plain strip-mall room, but locals call it Syracuse's best sushi. Fish quality beats the decor, so sit at the bar and order nigiri.
Armory Square kaiten bar since 2007: grab plates off the conveyor, with half-price belt sushi on many days.
The Utica area's go-to sushi bar, known for spicy crab rolls and a hibachi side for birthdays.
Penthouse steakhouse on top of the Turning Stone tower, with a sky-view balcony bar. It's a Forbes Four-Star and has been named the most romantic restaurant in NY.
Intimate farm-to-table room inside The Lodge at Turning Stone. It's Forbes Four-Star (2026) with a dress-up dress code, so it's the special-occasion pick.
Next to the Stanley Theatre, with a wine-tower bar, open kitchen, tapas and handmade gnocchi. The obvious pre-show dinner.
Utica's most-reviewed restaurant: a 24-oz Delmonico, red-sauce classics and house cannoli, served in a loud, big-city room.
The family behind Utica greens (1987) and an early claim to chicken riggies, now in a modern room on North Genesee. Order both.
Utica's oldest pizzeria (1914) and one of the oldest in the US. Come for upside-down pies and room-temp tomato pie on Bleecker St.
The half-moon cookie headquarters since 1955, with 10+ flavors and Utica-style tomato pie by the sheet.
Bagg's Square farm-to-table cooking with a seasonal, locally sourced menu, now on Main St. Pair it with a show at the Capitol or Stanley.
The 1988 Willow St. original: pit-smoked ribs and brisket, a biker-bar room, and live blues most nights.
Wood-fired, all-local seasonal cooking from James Beard–nominated chef Rich Strub, downtown Syracuse's top date-night table.
Armory Square institution famous for its hot tomato oil and stretch bread, with handmade pasta in a buzzy room.
Gilded Age mansion on Cazenovia Lake: scallops, octopus and a Wine Spectator–awarded list, with a lakeside terrace at sunset.
Cazenovia's 1835 inn, with fireplace dining upstairs and a stone-stepped tavern below for steaks and beef on weck.

chinese.s: Syracuse's Sichuan standard-bearer since 2012, with mala everything, hot pot burners built into the tables, and signature boiled fish in chili oil 水煮鱼.
Chengdu home cooking that's about more than heat. Get the hand-pulled pork dry noodles 干拌面 with egg-tomato.

chinese.n: Su Su Dim Sum 点心
chinese.s: Family-run since 2024 on East Brighton: dumplings, bao and crispy duck noodle soup over hand-pulled noodles in house duck broth.
University Hill hot pot and Sichuan kitchen: hot pot noodles, xiao long bao 小笼包, twice-cooked pork 回锅肉 and braised trotters.
Big round tables with lazy Susans, handmade dumplings and noodle bowls. Built for a group dinner, family style.

chinese.n: Asia Food Market 亚洲超市
chinese.s: The region's big Chinese supermarket: live seafood tanks, roast duck and pig 烧腊, produce, sauces and hot-pot fixings.
Taiwanese milk tea and milk-foam teas on the corner of Walton & Franklin in Armory Square.
Renovated pan-Asian market on Oneida St. serving Utica's Burmese, Chinese and SE Asian community, with a hot bar and taro or Thai-tea boba.

chinese.n: SU Spring Festival Gala 春晚
chinese.s: Syracuse University's Chinese Students & Scholars Association stages a Lunar New Year gala every February, with song, dance and xiangsheng 相声.

Downtown Syracuse kitchen by the hospitals doing traditional Sichuan and Northern Chinese cooking — grilled whole fish and beef skewers, plus dim sum. BYOB, wood-grain tables, open till 10:30 on weekends.
Family-run on Erie Blvd East since 1989 — Korean, Chinese and Japanese pantry staples plus house-made dumplings, tofu and rice cakes for a hot-pot night at home.

fishing.s: Oneida Lake's east-end shore: wade or cast the sand flats for walleye, perch and bass, and it's the go-to spot for ice fishing in winter. NY license required.
Walls and jetties where the Barge Canal and Fish Creek meet Oneida Lake. Walleye at dusk, perch and bass all summer, and the arcade and clam shacks a block away.
DEC's big hard-surface ramp on Oneida Lake's north shore (56 trailer spots, restrooms). Jig the shoals for walleye or work the weed edges for smallmouth and largemouth.
Onondaga County's paved launch at Brewerton on the lake's west end (fee), with room for 100 rigs. Walleye, yellow perch and bass, plus a beach for anyone who'd rather swim.
Nearly 28 miles of public fishing rights from Williamstown down to Blossvale. Stocked browns, the odd wild brookie, and quiet water ten minutes from the casino. NY license required.

The big one: king and coho salmon pack the river from mid-September into October, then steelhead and browns run all winter. Fly-fishing-only water up at Altmar. NY license required, and dress for crowds.
About 2½ miles of private, fee-access river below Pulaski: elbow room in peak salmon season, plus fall-through-spring steelhead and browns. Day passes and lodging on site.
Reservoir peninsula just north of Rome with a launch and shore access. Smallmouth, northern pike, walleye and bullhead, and campsites if you want a dawn start.
Big tailwater trout river below Trenton Falls, with the Kast Bridge stretch near Herkimer the classic. Browns and rainbows on dries in spring, and it's floatable. NY license required.
Capt. Jason runs Oneida Lake walleye and perch trips out of Constantia on a 21-ft Lund with LiveScope. Gear is included and he fillets your catch. Bring your own NY license.

biking.s: Onondaga County's 2,700-acre hilltop forest in Fabius, nicknamed the Adirondacks of CNY: roughly 20 miles of club-maintained singletrack and doubletrack. Mud season is real.
About 10 miles of multi-use trails through beech woods above two glacial meromictic lakes. Beginner-friendly, but stay off the hiker-only lake loops.
25-plus miles of rugged multi-use trail around the high point of Onondaga County, including the singletrack Onondaga Trail. Long climbs and rocky, technical descents.
About 13 miles of intermediate singletrack looping a pond near Nelson, just past Cazenovia. Rooty, flowy and usually quiet.
New Hartford town park with about 8 miles of mostly singletrack: ravines, stream crossings and plenty of dead ends. Signage is thin, so load a map first.
Old Forge ski hill with machine-built flow trails and rocky singletrack that link to Maple Ridge and town. The region's real descending, about 80 minutes north.
A 36-mile stone-dust towpath from DeWitt to Rome that runs right through Durhamville in the Town of Verona. Flat, easy gravel miles, and part of the Empire State Trail.
About 10 miles of singletrack on the college hill in Clinton, 20 minutes east: a flat, open spine trail with technical side trails jutting off it in every direction.
Ilion's 10-mile intermediate network of singletrack, double-track and fire road — start at the upper pavilion and work down through the Cemetery and North Ridge trails to the bottom of the park.
Fulton's 10-mile beginner-friendly web of singletrack and dirt roads — try them all, and expect mud in spring.

social.s: Syracuse's huge year-round market sheds: farmers, Amish bakers, Asian produce stalls and a crowd worth people-watching. Thursdays too, May to November.
Utica's year-round farmers market at Union Station: outdoors behind the station in summer, under the marble lobby's vaulted ceiling in winter.

social.n: Boots at the Brewery line dancing
social.s: Wednesday line dancing in Middle Ages Brewing's upstairs Music Hall: a taught warm-up, then open floor to country, pop and hip-hop, with crowds near 200.
Weekly taproom trivia at Syracuse's oldest brewery (since 1995). Grab a pint of Wailing Wench and a team.
Thursday trivia at a farm brewery north of Utica, about 25 minutes from Verona. Easy-going and local.
Syracuse's all-paces social run club, out year-round in any weather. Start spots rotate around the city, so check before you go.

social.n: Syracuse Track Club Green Lakes run
social.s: Thursday-evening group run from the Green Lakes disc-golf lot, on trails around the turquoise lakes. In winter it starts from Change of Pace on Grant Blvd instead.
Open Wednesday-evening group run from New Hartford's local running shop, listed with the Utica Roadrunners. All paces welcome.
Saturday-morning group run from Forte Strength & Fitness in New Hartford (back entrance), run by one of the most social running clubs in the Boilermaker's hometown.
CNY's West Coast Swing crew on the 3rd floor of the Ukrainian National Home — a 45-minute all-levels lesson at 7:15, then social dancing 8–10. No partner needed; first night free, then $1–5.
Free weekly trivia at Tipperary Hill's Irish pub, with prizes every week — sign up from 6, questions at 7.
Tuesdays & Thursdays from 6p with Syracuse Badminton Meetup [YMCA] at East Area Family YMCA, Fayetteville · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Meeple Monday: Board Games @ Harvey’s Garden
social.s: We love all kinds of tabletop games: heavy euros, fast and fun party games, new designer games, and the latest kickstarters. Mondays from 6p with Salt City Meeples at Harvey’s Garden, Syracuse · no Meetup fee.

remote.s: Small-town coworking at 155 Madison St in Oneida, the closest to Turning Stone. Flex members use the first-come workbench M–F 7a–6p; desk and office members get 24/7. Two bookable conference rooms (8 seats with TV/HDMI, 6 with a whiteboard), a couch-y collaboration room for calls, and a pantry with free coffee & tea. No day pass.

Griffiss Institute's innovation hub at 592 Hangar Rd (Suite 200) at Griffiss Business & Technology Park in Rome. Wi-Fi, free parking, a business print center, a free coffee bar and private lockers. M–F 8a–4p; monthly members get 24/7.

Mohawk Valley Community College's startup incubator at 326 Broad St, downtown Utica. Wi-Fi, a free coffee bar, lockers, filing cabinets, mail slots, copiers and printers. Day users M–F 8:30a–4:30p; members get a 24/7 digital key. The office rate needs a 12-month commitment.
remote.p: $20 day pass · $150/mo unlimited · office for two $425/mo
remote.b: Open floor doubles as event space; coworkers get warned of big events

remote.s: Village incubator at 8 Lebanon St in Hamilton, Colgate's hometown. Wi-Fi, free coffee & tea, kitchen, printing, lockers, mailbox service and whiteboards, plus mentorship and workshops. M–F 9a–5p; members get 24/7. Cheapest desk in the region.

In the Western Union Building at 351 S Warren St (Suite 2), downtown Syracuse. Wi-Fi, complimentary coffee, kitchen access and a game lounge; offices from $500/mo. M–F 8a–5p. Worth the Thruway run if you need a full city day.
remote.b: Reviewers call it always clean and quiet

remote.s: Downtown Utica at 303 Genesee St. Free Wi-Fi throughout the building and grounds 24/7, public PCs (1 hr a day; visitors from outside the Mid-York system get a guest pass with ID), b&w and color laser printers, Princh wireless printing and reservable meeting rooms. Mon–Thu 9–8, Fri 9–5, Sat 9:30–12:30, closed Sun.

447 S Salina St, downtown Syracuse (enter on Salina under the big library sign). Study areas on the 2nd floor, computers on the 1st and 3rd, wireless printing by email, app or web upload, a makerspace and meeting rooms by application. Mon 8:30–5, Tue–Wed 8:30–7:30, Thu–Fri 8:30–5, Sat 9–5, closed Sun. Nearby garages and Flowbird street parking.

The local roaster's café at 92 Genesee St in Bagg's Square, downtown Utica near Union Station. Fast Wi-Fi, laptops welcome and a cozy room. One of the area's most-reviewed coffee shops, it serves house-roasted coffee and a café menu with baked goods.
remote.b: Bustling downtown café; weekends busier than weekdays

remote.s: Syracuse roaster's downtown café at 401 S Salina St: fast Wi-Fi, abundant outlets and abundant seating, with laptops welcome, so it works for a full day. Open Mon–Fri 7a–7p and Sat–Sun 8a–6p, the longest hours of Kubal's cafés. The Central Library is a block away.
remote.b: Spacious, with ample seating and big windows

remote.s: Roaster café at 110 Harvard Pl in Syracuse's Westcott neighborhood, near Syracuse University: free, fast Wi-Fi and abundant, comfortable seating, plus a covered outdoor area the Wi-Fi reaches. Open 6a–10p weekdays and 7a–10p weekends, the latest hours of any work café in the region.
remote.b: Very popular on weekends; early mornings are calmest

iceskating.s: Syracuse's open-air downtown rink opens the day after Thanksgiving with the tree lighting and runs to early March. It's open daily (about 10/11a–8p, later on Fri/Sat). Admission is $5, or $3 for 55+ and kids, and rentals are $5. A Jan–Feb weekday lunch skate costs $6 and includes rental and cocoa. It's weather-dependent, so call 315-423-0129.

Syracuse's enclosed east-side city rink, the nearest of the three city rinks coming from Verona. Open skate runs Nov 1–Mar 31: Mon/Tue/Thu/Sun noon–4:30pm and Wed/Fri/Sat noon–8pm. It uses the same cheap city rates as Clinton Square ($5 adults, $3 seniors and kids, $5 rentals).

An enclosed, year-round city rink on Syracuse's South Side. Public open skate runs Nov 1–Mar 31, Tue–Fri noon–3pm. It's a quiet weekday option with the same city rates: $5 adults, $3 for 55+ and 12 and under, $5 skate rental, plus a small card fee if you pay by credit card.

Rome's city-run John F. Kennedy Civic Arena, about 20 minutes from Turning Stone. The November 2026 ice calendar lists public skates most weekdays 1–2:30pm, some 5–6:15pm sessions, and adult (19+) Skate-N-Shoot late mornings, fitted around youth hockey. Check the city's posted schedule for the week.

Utica's city-run outdoor rink on Memorial Parkway. Last season it opened Nov 28 and ran Wed–Fri 4–9p, Sat noon–4p and 6–9p, and Sun noon–4p, with $5 admission and $5 rentals, plus a Skate with Santa day. The city hadn't posted a 2026–27 opening date as of early November. Call the Mayor's office for weather closures.

The Town of Whitestown's year-round 200x85 ft sheet in Whitesboro has a pro shop with skate rentals. Public skate costs $5, plus $5 for rentals, and the town's 2026 monthly flyers set weekend sessions. Helmets and gloves are required for the separate Skate n Shoot. It's a short hop off Thruway exit 32 and reliable ice even in summer.

skating.s: 2.2 miles of wide, mostly flat pavement between Canastota (S Peterboro St) and Wampsville, opened in 2019. That makes it rare paving in a region of gravel towpaths, about 15 minutes from Turning Stone. It parallels the active CSX line, with an overlook pavilion built from old rails, and it links to the Erie Canalway in Canastota.

skating.n: Onondaga Lake East Shore Recreation Trail
skating.s: A 20-ft-wide paved path in Onondaga Lake Park, built for in-line skating and bikes and running about 2.5 miles along the lake. From April to October walkers must keep to the edge and dogs are barred. Trams use the centerline. It connects to the 4.5-mile paved West Shore Trail past Lakeview Amphitheater.

The Philip A. Rayhill Memorial Trail: about 5 miles of asphalt on an old New York Central bed, roughly following Judd Rd. An extension runs along Sauquoit Creek into New York Mills. Trailheads are on New Hartford St and at the end of Clinton St. The far western end, past Halsey Rd, is narrower and less maintained.

A flat, 3.8-mile asphalt and concrete path through shaded riverside woods along the Mohawk, from Beacon St to Haselton-Wright Park. From Bellamy Harbor Park on the Erie Canal you reach it via the Erie Blvd sidewalk past Fort Stanwix. The southern end ties into the Erie Canalway, so you can extend the skate along the canal.

Rome's roller rink on Ridge St, the nearest wheels-on-wood option to Verona. Weekend sessions are Sat 1–4p and 7–10p and Sun 1–4p, with extra 12–4p skates over school breaks and separate Wednesday and Friday night sessions. Skate rental is paid at admission. Its Kids Skate Free passes cover children 10 and under at weekend sessions.

A roller rink north of Syracuse that rents both quad and inline (hockey-style) skates, up to size 13 in inlines. Sessions are Wed 6:30–9p ($10), Sat–Sun 1–3:30p ($12) and Fri–Sat 7–10p ($15), and rentals are $5. Saturday-morning group lessons and speed practice run before the tiny-tots session. Bringing your own skates is welcome.

Syracuse's 4.8-mi creekside path is entirely paved and off-road, and it was designed for cyclists, skaters and walkers. It runs from the South Side through Armory Square and on to Onondaga Lake, linking there to the lakeshore trails for a longer day. Several road crossings break up the downtown stretch, so the lake end is the better roll.
